class.name: BulletFactory2D
class.brief_description: The heart of the BlastBullets2D plugin. Use this node to spawn bullets.
class.description:
The factory does all the work in spawning bullets and configuring other plugin related options. Keep a reference of your [b]BulletFactory2D[/b] node throughout the lifetime of your game and call the functions you need.
For tutorials and usage examples: [url=https://www.youtube.com/@realnikich]YouTube Channel[/url] [url=https://github.com/nikoladevelops/godot-blast-bullets-2d]Official Repository Of BlastBullets2D[/url]
[b]This plugin is completely free and open source - created by [url=https://x.com/realNikich]realNikich[/url][/b] Support My Work [url=https://ko-fi.com/realnikich]Donate On Ko-fi[/url] [url=https://www.patreon.com/realnikich]Donate On Patreon[/url]

method.name: debug_get_active_attachments_amount
method.description: Get the amount of active [BulletAttachment2D] nodes.

method.name: debug_get_active_bullets_amount
method.description: Get the amount of active bullet multimeshes of a specific type.

method.name: debug_get_attachments_pool_amount
method.description: Get the amount of [BulletAttachment2D] inside the object pool.

method.name: debug_get_attachments_pool_info
method.description: Get the whole information about the attachment object pool. Returns a [Dictionary] containing the scene path (or [code]"<in-memory>"[/code] for unsaved scenes) as the KEY and the amount of pooled attachments from that scene as the VALUE.

method.name: debug_get_bullets_pool_amount
method.description: Get the amount of bullet multimeshes of a specific type currently in the object pool.

method.name: debug_get_bullets_pool_info
method.description: Get the whole information about the bullet multimeshes object pool of a specific type. Returns a [Dictionary] containing [MultiMeshPoolKey2D] as the KEY (one per exact amount_bullets + shape bucket) and the amount of pooled multimeshes in that bucket as the VALUE.

method.name: debug_get_total_attachments_amount
method.description: Get the total amount of [BulletAttachment2D] in the scene tree.

method.name: debug_get_total_bullets_amount
method.description: Get the total amount of bullet multimeshes of a specific type in the scene tree.

method.name: free_active_bullets
method.description: Frees active bullets in the scene tree. Pass [code]null[/code] (default) to free all, or a [MultiMeshPoolKey2D] to free only that exact amount_bullets + shape bucket. Refused during the physics step (for example inside collision handlers); call it deferred then.

method.name: free_attachments_pool
method.description: Completely frees the [BulletAttachment2D] object pool. To free only the attachments that came from one scene, use [method free_attachments_pool_for_scene].

method.name: free_attachments_pool_for_scene
method.description: Frees only the pooled [BulletAttachment2D] attachments that came from the given scene.

method.name: free_bullets_pool
method.description: Frees the object pool of a particular bullet type. Pass [code]null[/code] (default) to free the whole pool, or a [MultiMeshPoolKey2D] to free only that exact amount_bullets + shape bucket. Example: [code]MultiMeshPoolKey2D.make(200, PhysicsServer2D.SHAPE_CIRCLE)[/code]. Refused during the physics step; call it deferred then.

method.name: free_disabled_bullets
method.description: Frees disabled (pooled) bullets. Pass [code]null[/code] (default) to free all, or a [MultiMeshPoolKey2D] to free only that exact amount_bullets + shape bucket. Refused during the physics step; call it deferred then.

method.name: get_is_factory_busy
method.description: Sometimes the [b]BulletFactory2D[/b] might be busy doing some important work. This property provides an easy way to check if that's true.

method.name: get_is_tearing_down
method.description: Returns true once the factory started destroying itself. While true, teardown paths stop touching child nodes and most factory operations report an error instead of running.

method.name: get_physics_space
method.description: Get the physics world space in which the bullets interact.

method.name: helper_generate_transforms_aimed
method.description: Generates a fan of transforms aimed from the marker at [code]target_position[/code]. Same as [method helper_generate_transforms_fan] with the cone centered on the marker to target direction. Useful for aimed bursts and shotgun spreads that track a player. Returns an empty array if the target coincides with the marker.

method.name: helper_generate_transforms_fan
method.description: Generates a fan of transforms spread evenly across a cone. [code]direction_angle[/code] is the cone center relative to the marker rotation, [code]spread[/code] is the full cone width in radians, and [code]step_offset[/code] staggers origins along the direction so pellets do not stack on top of each other. A single bullet flies straight down the cone center. Useful for shotgun spreads.

method.name: helper_generate_transforms_grid
method.description: Generates a grid of transforms that are positioned relative to the [code]marker_transform[/code].

method.name: helper_generate_transforms_line
method.description: Generates transforms in a straight wall centered on the marker along [code]direction[/code], spaced evenly by [code]spacing[/code]. Bullets face along the line when [code]face_direction[/code] is true, otherwise they keep the marker rotation. Useful for walls, curtains and gates. Returns an empty array when the direction is zero.

method.name: helper_generate_transforms_ring
method.description: Generates transforms placed evenly on a ring (or arc, when [code]arc[/code] is smaller than a full turn) around the marker. Every bullet faces outward, so art drawn facing right travels away from the center. Set [code]face_outward[/code] to false for implosion patterns that fly toward the center. Useful for radial bursts and boss rings.

method.name: helper_generate_transforms_spiral
method.description: Generates transforms along an expanding spiral around the marker, each bullet facing outward. Useful for rotating emitter looks and volute patterns.

method.name: populate_attachments_pool
method.description: Populates the attachments object pool. Ensure that the [code]attachment_scene[/code] contains an actual [BulletAttachment2D] scene where you attach other nodes - particles or anything else you could think of. Pooling is keyed by the scene itself, so every loader of the same scene shares one pool bucket.

method.name: populate_bullets_pool
method.description: Pre-creates [code]instance_count[/code] disabled multimeshes in one exact bucket. [code]key.amount_bullets[/code] is bullets per multimesh (must equal [code]multimesh_data[/code] transforms size); [code]instance_count[/code] is how many multimeshes to create. The [code]key[/code] is required and must match the bucket derived from [code]multimesh_data[/code] (amount_bullets + effective collision shape); mismatch aborts with an error and creates nothing. Example: [code]populate_bullets_pool(MultiMeshPoolKey2D.make(5, PhysicsServer2D.SHAPE_CIRCLE), data, 2)[/code] creates 2 multimeshes of 5 bullets each.

method.name: reactivate_multimesh_instance
method.description: Re-registers a pooled multimesh inside the factory's active set after one of its bullets was woken with enable_bullet() outside of a normal spawn. Does nothing when the multimesh is already active, when the factory is busy, or when the factory is tearing down. You normally never call this yourself, enable_bullet() already handles it.

method.name: reset
method.description: Resets the factory. Pass [code]null[/code] (default) for a full reset (all bullets, pools, and the full attachment pool). Pass a [MultiMeshPoolKey2D] to reset only that exact amount_bullets+shape bucket; unrelated pooled attachments are preserved. Refused during the physics step; call it deferred then. Emits the [signal reset_finished] signal when complete.

method.name: set_physics_space
method.description: Sets the world physics space that the bullets interact in. Set it before spawning: it applies to subsequently spawned bullets, already spawned areas stay in their space. Invalid RIDs are rejected with an error.

method.name: set_use_physics_interpolation_editor
method.description: Editor-side setter behind the [member use_physics_interpolation] property. At runtime always use [method set_use_physics_interpolation_runtime] instead.

method.name: set_use_physics_interpolation_runtime
method.description: Controls whether physics interpolation is enabled or not for all bullets controlled by the [b]BulletFactory2D[/b]. This method is supposed to be called during runtime, while the [method set_use_physics_interpolation_editor] method is supposed to be called in the editor.

method.name: spawn_block_bullets
method.description: Spawns [BlockBullets2D] - bullets that act as a block that travels in a single direction with the same speed. If there is already a multimesh available in the object pool (that matches the amount of transforms provided and the collision shape) then it gets re-used with the new data. These bullets can NOT be controlled individually, but they are more efficient performance wise.

method.name: spawn_controllable_directional_bullets
method.description:
Spawns DirectionalBullets2D that are meant to be controlled and edited. If there is a multimesh available in the object pool (that matches the amount of transforms provided and the collision shape) then it gets re-used with the new data. Use if you want homing bullets or to edit properties during runtime.
Warning: Since object pooling is enabled by default, if you save these bullets to an array you might accidentally push the exact same multimesh (you end up with 2 references or more to the same exact object), that's why it's smart to disable auto pooling if you are storing them in arrays or other data structures - that way you can even implement your own pooling system.

method.name: spawn_directional_bullets
method.description: Spawns [DirectionalBullets2D] - bullets that have individual directions determined by the rotation of their transforms. If there is already a multimesh available in the object pool (that matches the amount of transforms provided and the collision shape) then it gets re-used with the new data. To control these bullets individually, use the [method spawn_controllable_directional_bullets] function instead.

method.name: teleport_shift_all_bullets
method.description: Shifts all directional bullets in the scene by a certain amount (only bullets spawned by this particular [b]BulletFactory2D[/b]). Block bullets are not affected (a warning is emitted when any exist and are skipped).

members.member: The color for the collision shapes of all [BlockBullets2D].
The color for the collision shapes of all [DirectionalBullets2D].
Whether the debugger of the collision shapes is enabled or not.
Use this if you want to pause processing of bullets - being able to stop bullets in place. Always use this instead of [code]set_process[/code]/[code]set_physics_process[/code].

Determines whether physics interpolation is enabled or not. The setter is for the editor only.
Instead always use [method set_use_physics_interpolation_runtime] if you are doing changes during runtime.

signal.name: block_area_entered
signal.description: Emitted synchronously in the physics tick when a block bullet enters a physics area. Same handler contract as [signal directional_area_entered].

signal.name: block_body_entered
signal.description: Emitted synchronously in the physics tick when a block bullet enters a physics body. Same handler contract as [signal directional_body_entered].

signal.name: block_life_time_over
signal.description: Emitted (deferred, outside the physics step) when a block bullet multimesh's lifetime is over, but only if the [MultiMeshBulletsData2D]'s [member MultiMeshBulletsData2D.is_life_time_over_signal_enabled] is set to [code]true[/code].

signal.name: directional_area_entered
signal.description: Emitted synchronously in the physics tick when a directional bullet enters a physics area. Handlers run with live instance state (no casts needed); custom data and transforms are one instance call away (bullet_get_custom_data(), get_bullet_global_transform()). Only structural factory calls (reset/free_*/populate_*) must be deferred - the error message says so when it happens.

signal.name: directional_body_entered
signal.description:
Emitted synchronously in the physics tick when a directional bullet enters a physics body.
Note: Static bodies can be detected by the bullets, but only if you set the [MultiMeshBulletsData2D]'s [member MultiMeshBulletsData2D.monitorable] property to [code]true[/code] when spawning bullets - this is at the cost of performance of course, so it's better to stick with [Area2D] or other types of bodies for enemies/buildings etc and leave the [member MultiMeshBulletsData2D.monitorable] property to be false.

signal.name: directional_life_time_over
signal.description: Emitted (deferred, outside the physics step) when a directional bullet multimesh's lifetime is over, but only if the [MultiMeshBulletsData2D]'s [member MultiMeshBulletsData2D.is_life_time_over_signal_enabled] is set to [code]true[/code].

signal.name: reset_finished
signal.description: Emitted when the [method reset] method finishes.
